## Source and installation

The source repository is [apoorvalal/trex](https://github.com/apoorvalal/trex).
Install it from GitHub into an environment with an appropriate PyTorch build;
the unrelated package named `trex` on PyPI is not this library. The [installation
guide](start/installation.qmd) describes both editable and commit-pinned use.

## Build the site

Install **Quarto 1.8.27** and the Python documentation extra. Use the same
Python environment for the package, Quartodoc and executable examples:

```bash
python -m pip install -e '.[docs]'
python docs/build.py
```

The builder generates API pages with Quartodoc, checks coverage of public
exports, records the source revision and environment, executes the vignettes,
renders the website, and checks internal links and assets. Output goes to
`docs/_site/`; it is not committed to the source branch. During writing:

```bash
python docs/build.py --api-only
quarto preview docs
```

Preview is not a substitute for the final executable build. All lightweight
examples use explicit seeds and the CPU. The optional LLM guide is labeled
non-executed and does not download model weights. Figures and printed tables
on the other worked pages are produced by their code, not copied manually.
CI additionally checks every page in Chromium at desktop and mobile widths,
including equation rendering, search, theme switching and sidebar navigation.

## How publication works

Source lives on `main`; generated HTML and assets live on **`gh-pages`**.
The `docs` GitHub Actions workflow builds and checks pull requests without
publishing. A successful build on `main` (or a manual workflow run on `main`)
commits the rendered site to `gh-pages` and deploys the same files through
GitHub Pages. This explicit deploy step avoids relying on a second workflow
being triggered by an Actions-authored branch push.

Do not hand-edit `gh-pages`: edit `.qmd` files or Python docstrings on a source
branch. Once merged to `main`, the site is rebuilt automatically. The published
[build record](build-info.json) identifies its source commit, build time and
key dependency versions. The `gh-pages` commit message also records the source
revision, so rendered changes remain inspectable and recoverable.

## Adding or changing an estimator

1. Document its input shapes, objective, normalization, fitted attributes and
   failure conditions in source docstrings. Make supported inference explicit.
2. Add its public entry point to the Quartodoc inventory in `_quarto.yml`.
   The build rejects omissions from the package's declared public exports.
3. Add a mathematical guide or extend an existing one. Include a small
   reproducible example, a relevant diagnostic and an explanation of the
   assumptions needed to interpret the estimate.
4. Add numerical tests that address the estimator, preferably with independent
   reference calculations, and run the affected tests. For broader changes run
   the repository suite with the test extra installed.
5. Run the documentation build. Inspect plots and formulas as well as exit
   status; a successful optimizer call need not be an informative example.

## Documentation design

The site uses local/shared Quarto assets and KaTeX for mathematics. It is a
multipage website, so shared assets avoid duplicating large scripts in every
API page. No external font service is required. The sidebar, search and
method-selection page provide complementary ways to find material.

The API reference is generated from the installed checkout, including
inherited public methods. A displayed inherited method can still be
unimplemented for a particular estimator: consult the method body/docstring
and the guide's inference notes. Research interfaces and numerical behavior
can evolve; pin a commit and environment for a reproducible study.
